summary: Audit scripts/heavy_machines for Windows (PowerShell, pip Isaac Sim) failures, then adversarially verify each finding

findings.snippet: print(f"[scenario] recording {sc.n_frames} frames at {sc.fps} fps ({args_cli.renderer}) → {out}", flush=True)
findings.mechanism: U+2192 is not in cp1252. On Windows a console stdout is UTF-8 (PEP 528), but a redirected or piped stdout falls back to locale.getpreferredencoding(), which is cp1252 on an English install (cp1256 on a Persian one), with errors='strict'. The print raises UnicodeEncodeError. I reproduced it with PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 ("'charmap' codec can't encode character '→'"). The em dashes elsewhere are fine because U+2014 is 0x97 in cp1252.
findings.failure_scenario: The PowerShell command is run as `isaaclab.bat -p scripts\heavy_machines\scenarios\render_scenario.py --scenario adt_approach_hex --headless *> log.txt`, or piped through Tee-Object, which is the normal way to capture a long path-traced render. Kit starts, the 40-frame warm-up and the asset-streaming loop run, then this print raises. The traceback appears before frame 0 is recorded, and nothing is written. The exception leaves main() before `os._exit` at line 258, so Kit teardown can hang or crash (the script's own comment on line 257 says close() can hang). Run interactively in a console it works, so this only shows up when output is captured.
findings.fix: Make stdout and stderr tolerant at the top of the script, before any print, which changes nothing on Linux or UTF-8 consoles: `for _s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):\n    try: _s.reconfigure(errors="replace")\n    except Exception: pass`. Alternatively replace the '→' in the print with '->'. A zero-code workaround is `$env:PYTHONUTF8='1'` in PowerShell before launching; the bake child and spawn workers inherit it.

findings.snippet: log(f"[bake] done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s → {tex_dir}")
findings.mechanism: Same cp1252 stdout failure as the render_scenario.py finding. bake.py runs as a child process of render_scenario.py (subprocess.run(cmd) at line 70), so it inherits the parent's redirected stdout. This log call comes after the manifest has already been written at lines 198-199.
findings.failure_scenario: With output redirected, the first run bakes every texture and writes manifest.json, then dies with UnicodeEncodeError. The child returns exit code 1, render_scenario prints '[scenario] texture bake FAILED' and calls sys.exit(3). Several minutes of baking look like a failure even though the cache is complete. The second run takes the '[bake] cache hit' path, which is ASCII, and then hits the render_scenario.py:235 crash. Direct use of `python scripts\heavy_machines\scenarios\bake.py ... > bake.log` fails the same way.
findings.fix: Add the same `sys.stdout.reconfigure(errors="replace")` guard at the top of bake.main(), or change '→' to '->'. Setting PYTHONUTF8=1 also covers it.

findings.snippet: print(f"[demo] {spec.display_name}: {len(script)} phases, {total} steps → {out_dir}", flush=True)
findings.mechanism: Same cp1252 stdout encoding failure when stdout is redirected. Other non-cp1252 literals that are printed at runtime are collect_machine.py:211 (`print(f"[done] {args_cli.num_episodes} episodes → {out_dir}", flush=True)`), collect_machine.py:36 (the argparse description, shown only for --help) and the '≥' in the message at checks.py:360 (shown only when that check fires).
findings.failure_scenario: scripted_demo.py with redirected output crashes at this print before state.csv or any frame is written. collect_machine.py:211 runs after every episode and bag has been written; it raises inside main(), the `except BaseException` handler prints a traceback, and the script exits with code 1 although the data is complete.
findings.fix: Use the same reconfigure(errors='replace') guard at the top of each entry script, or replace '→' with '->' in those literals.

findings.snippet: print("[scenario] ffmpeg not found — encode with:\n  " + " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
findings.mechanism: ffmpeg is not shipped with Windows and is not in Isaac Lab's install_requires (I grepped setup.py), so on a fresh PC this fallback branch is the expected path. The hint is a bare `" ".join(cmd)` with no quoting. In PowerShell, an unquoted `-vf scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p` is parsed with the comma as the array operator, so ffmpeg receives a mangled filter argument. Any path with a space (for example C:\Users\Ali Cheraghi\...\frame_%05d.png) is split into several arguments. subprocess.list2cmdline quotes only the space case, so it is not enough either.
findings.failure_scenario: All frames are rendered, then the script prints the hint and exits with code 1. The user pastes the line into PowerShell and ffmpeg fails with a filter-graph parse error or 'No such file', so the finished render looks broken.
findings.fix: Print the arguments quoted, which is still valid in bash: `print("...encode with:\n  ffmpeg " + " ".join('"%s"' % a for a in cmd[1:]), flush=True)`. Or use shlex.quote when os.name != 'nt' and double quotes on nt. Optionally add `imageio-ffmpeg` to the Windows setup instructions so the fallback is not reached.

findings.snippet: os.remove(old)
findings.mechanism: Python's os.remove maps to DeleteFileW, which fails on Windows with PermissionError [WinError 32] if any other process holds the file open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Linux unlinks regardless. The same applies to the previous <scenario>_<camera>.mp4, which ffmpeg `-y` must reopen for writing at the end of the run (line 140).
findings.failure_scenario: The user iterates on the same scenario and has a frame from the last run open in an image viewer or the Explorer preview pane. The second run raises PermissionError at line 227 after the minutes-long warm-up and before recording, with no hint to close the file. If instead the previous .mp4 is open in a video player, the whole path-traced render finishes and ffmpeg then fails with 'Permission denied'. The script prints only '[scenario] ffmpeg FAILED for ...' and exits 1. The frames survive. This depends on a third-party app holding the file, so it is intermittent.
findings.fix: Wrap the delete: `try: os.remove(old)\nexcept OSError as exc: print(f"[scenario] could not remove {old}: {exc}", flush=True)`. The frames are overwritten anyway, so deleting only indices >= n_frames would suffice. Optionally print the ffmpeg return code and 'is the old mp4 open in a player?' when write_video fails. Linux behaviour is unchanged.

findings.snippet:
with open(path) as f:
                old = f.read()
        if old != text:
            with open(path, "w") as f:
                f.write(text)
findings.mechanism: open() defaults to cp1252 on Windows, and "\n" is written as "\r\n". build_urdf() puts an em dash (U+2014) in the header comment ('generated by ... machines/<name>.py — do not edit by hand'), and all 18 committed assets/heavy_machines/*/*.urdf contain it as UTF-8 bytes E2 80 94. Read as cp1252 these come back as 'â€”' style mojibake, so `old != text` is always true. The file is rewritten with the dash as the single byte 0x97 and with CRLF line endings. The JSON sidecars are unaffected because json.dumps escapes non-ASCII.
findings.failure_scenario: The first run of anything that builds a machine articulation (HeavyMachineEnv via machine_env.articulation_cfg, scripted_demo, collect_machine, teleop, showcase) or `check_machine.py` rewrites the machine's tracked URDF. I simulated cp1252 and CRLF writes on a scratch copy of assets/heavy_machines: 18 of 36 files were rewritten (every URDF), each now with byte 0x97. `git status` shows the URDFs modified, the file is no longer valid UTF-8, and a strict parser rejects it (expat: 'not well-formed (invalid token): line 2, column 90'). I could not verify whether Isaac Sim's URDF importer tolerates the stray byte. The UrdfConverter content hash also changes, which forces a re-import. test/test_machines.py::test_committed_assets_in_sync (line 54, `with open(urdf) as f:`) fails for every machine for the same reason, until its open() gets encoding='utf-8' too. The primary render path (render_scenario.py) never calls write_assets.
findings.fix: Use `with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:` for the read and `with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:` for the write. Linux output is byte-identical, and a CRLF checkout (autocrlf=true) still compares equal because reads use universal newlines. Apply the same encoding to the open() calls in test/test_machines.py lines 54 and 56. Workaround without code changes: `$env:PYTHONUTF8='1'`.

findings.snippet: (out_dir / f"{spec.name}.urdf").write_text(build_urdf(spec))
findings.mechanism: Path.write_text() without encoding uses cp1252 on Windows and translates "\n" to "\r\n". The URDF text contains an em dash, so the file gets byte 0x97, which is invalid UTF-8. The same applies to line 183, `(out_dir / "qos_overrides.yaml").write_text(qos_overrides_yaml())`, which only gains CRLF.
findings.failure_scenario: The <out>/<machine>.urdf written next to the bags is not valid UTF-8, so strict XML tools or editors that assume UTF-8 reject or mangle it. The /robot_description topic inside the bag is unaffected, because rosbags serialises the Python str as UTF-8.
findings.fix: `write_text(build_urdf(spec), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` (Path.write_text accepts newline= from Python 3.10, and the venv is 3.11). Do the same for the yaml line. Linux output is identical.

findings.snippet:
with open(path) as f:
            text = f.read()
findings.mechanism: `check_machine.py --readme` reads and rewrites README.md with the default cp1252 encoding. The existing UTF-8 README is read as mojibake and written back as the same bytes, so untouched text round-trips. But the regenerated table rows contain 'ö' (Vögele), '³' (9 m³ transit mixer) and '—' (the no-tools fallback), which are written as the single bytes 0xF6, 0xB3 and 0x97. Line 47 `with open(path, "w") as f:` also converts every "\n" to "\r\n".
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows, `--readme` leaves README.md as mixed-encoding invalid UTF-8 (simulated: "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb3 in position 2218") with 173 CRLF lines, where an LF checkout had none. GitHub and editors show replacement characters in the table, and `git diff` marks the whole file as changed if autocrlf is off.
findings.fix: Use `open(path, encoding="utf-8")` for the read and `open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` for the write. Linux behaviour is identical.

findings.snippet: print(f"  wrote   {os.path.relpath(urdf)} , {os.path.relpath(meta)}")
findings.mechanism: On Windows os.path.relpath raises ValueError when the path and the current directory are on different drives (checked with ntpath: "path is on mount 'F:', start on mount 'C:'"). The asset paths are always under the repo's drive (F:), but PowerShell usually starts in C:\Users\<name>.
findings.failure_scenario: The user runs `python F:\Projects\IsaacLab\scripts\heavy_machines\check_machine.py` from a C: working directory. The first machine's files are written, then check_machine.py aborts with an uncaught ValueError. The remaining machines are neither validated nor regenerated, and the exit code is nonzero.
findings.fix: Add a helper `def _rel(p):\n    try: return os.path.relpath(p)\n    except ValueError: return p` and use it in the print. Linux output is unchanged.

REPORT-ONLY: no repository file was edited. Scratch files are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vla-datagen/39bfe37a-c345-5663-b8fb-e785cd7a1b70/scratchpad/wincompat/ (scan_nonascii.py, scan_str.py, sim_write_assets.py, sim_readme.py, assets_copy/).

CHECKED AND NOT REPORTED (no concrete Windows failure found):
- Texture file names: save_texture_set uses f"{machine}_{material}_{albedo|roughness|normal}.png", terrain_{near|local|far}_*.png and rock_{0..2}_*.png. The key 'machine:<m>:<mat>' is only a manifest dict key, never a file name. I enumerated the 19 machine/material jobs for adt_approach_hex: no illegal characters (<>:"|?*), no reserved device names, no case-insensitive collisions. No timestamps appear in any file name.
- MAX_PATH: the longest generated texture path is about 111 characters under F:\Projects\IsaacLab\heavy_machine_videos\adt_approach_hex\textures. Frames, the usd_dir cache and the LeRobot output are also well under 260.
- manifest.json: json.dump uses ensure_ascii=True, so it is pure ASCII and the cp1252 default open() in bake.py lines 163 and 198 round-trips even for a non-ASCII user profile path. The cache-hit check os.path.exists() on stored paths simply misses (and rebakes) if the folder came from WSL or Linux, so there is no failure.
- Asset paths in USD: bake.py stores os.path.join(...) paths, so on Windows they are F:\...\x.png with backslashes. usd_scene._texture passes them as str to Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Asset. With usd-core 0.26.8 I confirmed Sdf.AssetPath keeps the string verbatim (no normalisation), and an exported .usda (@F:\...@) re-imports identically. The stage is only authored in memory and never exported. I believe omni.client/OmniUsdResolver normalises 'F:\...' paths, but I could not test inside Kit, so I did not list it as a failure. If textures ever show as default grey on Windows, the cheap hardening is `file = file.replace(chr(92), '/')` in usd_scene._texture (and pass `Path(p).as_posix()` in bake), which is a no-op on Linux. Sky HDR and Nucleus paths are built with '/' URLs, not os.path.
- np.load in bake.load_scatter is not in a `with`, but the NpzFile is a local that CPython closes on return, and arrays are read eagerly, so there is no open handle when rocks.npz is rewritten. There is no os.rename, shutil.rmtree of live files, NamedTemporaryFile, mmap or PIL.Image.open anywhere outside tests. In tests, PIL handles use `with`.
- scripted_demo.py already uses `open(..., newline="")` for the csv. summary.jsonl lines are ASCII (json.dumps default), and CRLF there is harmless.
- bake.py as `__main__` plus spawn workers: it has an `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard, the `__package__` fix-up works when re-run as __mp_main__, and jobs and SceneOptions pickle by reference to __main__. This is the same as Linux spawn.
- Output paths: `--out` default 'heavy_machine_videos/{scenario}' goes through abspath, which normalises slashes, and subprocess is called with list arguments, so spaces are fine. expanduser works via USERPROFILE.
- The URDFs use primitive geometry only, so there are no mesh/package:// path issues. ASSET_ROOT is built with os.path.join/abspath. The spec strings (display_name, reference, description) contain only ö ³ ± ° × – and so on, all encodable in cp1252, and they only reach JSON (ensure_ascii) or prints. Nothing in the spec fields breaks stdout encoding; only the literal '→' prints listed above do.

ENV-LEVEL WORKAROUND (no code change): set `$env:PYTHONUTF8 = '1'` in PowerShell before launching. It switches open() and redirected stdout to UTF-8 for the process and its bake/spawn children, which fixes the stdout and open()-encoding findings (not the cross-drive relpath, ffmpeg hint or file-lock ones). Newline translation to CRLF remains and only matters for check_machine --readme and the written URDFs.

OUT-OF-LENS OBSERVATIONS (mechanism concrete, not filesystem/text I/O):
- bake.py:185 `cf.ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers, ...)` with render_scenario.py:47 default `--bake_workers = os.cpu_count()-1`. On Windows ProcessPoolExecutor raises ValueError('max_workers must be <= 61') (concurrent.futures.process._MAX_WINDOWS_WORKERS = 61). A machine with 63 or more logical CPUs crashes in the bake before anything is baked. Fix: `min(61, ...)` for the default, or pass --bake_workers 16.
- source/isaaclab/setup.py pins numpy<2, so on Windows the default integer (astype(int), np.arange) is 32-bit. I skimmed the integer-hash code (rocks.py:116-119 masks to 32 bits and appears wrap-safe) and found no concrete failure, but other lenses should look at astype(int) index math.
- User-facing launch note from the original transcript: in PowerShell, `.venv\Scripts\activate` runs activate.bat in a child cmd, so the environment change does not persist. Use `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` (may need `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`). Isaac Lab's isaaclab.bat needs VIRTUAL_ENV to find the venv's python. Run it from F:\Projects\IsaacLab as `isaaclab.bat -p scripts\heavy_machines\scenarios\render_scenario.py --scenario adt_approach_hex --headless`. Also install ffmpeg (for example `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`) or `pip install imageio-ffmpeg`, otherwise the render ends with exit code 1 and only the unquoted ffmpeg hint (see the ffmpeg-hint finding). WSL is not needed. The earlier WSL failure came from running ./isaaclab.sh against a Windows-layout .venv (Scripts\ not bin/) with no _isaac_sim.

verdicts.reason: Snippet matches render_scenario.py:235. The mechanism is real and I reproduced the codec behaviour: PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 turns print('a → b') into UnicodeEncodeError ('charmap' codec can't encode '→'). U+2192 is also missing from cp1256 and cp1250, so a Persian ACP does not help. U+2014 encodes to 0x97 in all three, so the em dashes are safe. Python 3.11 on Windows uses UTF-8 only for an interactive console (PEP 528). A redirected or piped stdout gets the ANSI code page with errors='strict', and UTF-8 mode is not the default until 3.15. isaaclab.bat does not pipe the child, and I found no stdout reconfiguration in isaaclab/app (AppLauncher only swaps in devnull temporarily and restores sys.__stdout__). Caveat on severity: this does NOT trigger for the user's literal command, which has no redirect. It triggers only with `*>`, `> file`, `| Tee-Object`, or an IDE or CI runner that pipes stdout. The claim that Kit teardown may hang after the exception is plausible but unverified. Without os._exit, interpreter shutdown with Kit still loaded can hang.
verdicts.fix: At the top of render_scenario.py, before run_bake() and any print: `for _s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):\n    try: _s.reconfigure(errors="replace")\n    except Exception: pass`. It mutates the same TextIOWrapper that AppLauncher later restores via sys.__stdout__, and it is a no-op on UTF-8 terminals, so Linux is unchanged. Equivalent: replace the '→' with '->' in the f-string. The bake child needs its own guard (see the bake finding). Environment workaround: $env:PYTHONUTF8='1'.

verdicts.reason: Snippet matches bake.py:200. The manifest is written at lines 198-199 and the arrow log follows, so a redirected run leaves a complete cache and then exits 1. render_scenario.run_bake treats returncode != 0 as 'texture bake FAILED' and calls sys.exit(3). On the rerun, the 'cache hit' log is ASCII, so the failure moves to render_scenario.py:235. The child inherits the parent's redirected handle and picks its own ANSI encoding. The other bake logs ('[bake] N rocks', '{machine} / {material}', 'colour {ppm} px/m') are ASCII, so the arrow is the only trigger. It does not fire in an interactive console.
verdicts.fix: In bake.main() (or at the top of the __main__ block), before bake_assets: `for _s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):\n    try: _s.reconfigure(errors="replace")\n    except Exception: pass`. findings.snippet: log(f"[bake] done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s → {tex_dir}")
findings.mechanism: U+2192 is not in cp1252 (or any Windows ANSI code page). On Windows, Python 3.11 only uses the UTF-8-capable console API when stdout is an interactive console. When stdout is a pipe or file (PowerShell `> log.txt`, `| Tee-Object`, an IDE/CI capture) it uses the ANSI code page, normally cp1252, with the 'strict' error handler. The bake child inherits the parent's redirected stdout, so print() raises UnicodeEncodeError. This is the last statement of bake_assets(), and it runs AFTER manifest.json has been written (lines 197-199).
findings.failure_scenario: `.\isaaclab.bat -p scripts\heavy_machines\scenarios\render_scenario.py --scenario adt_approach_hex --headless 2>&1 | Tee-Object render.log`, first run with a cold cache. Every texture bakes (minutes), manifest.json is written, then the child dies with `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '→'` and exit code 1. render_scenario.run_bake() prints `[scenario] texture bake FAILED` and sys.exit(3), so Kit never starts. A second identical run is a cache hit (the message is ASCII) and works, which is very confusing. Reproduced on Linux: `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python bake.py ... | cat` gave exit=1 with manifest.json present, and the rerun printed `cache hit` and exited 0. A plain interactive PowerShell console is not affected.
findings.fix: Use ASCII in the message: `log(f"[bake] done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s -> {tex_dir}")`. Optionally add at the top of bake.main(): `for _s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):\n    if hasattr(_s, 'reconfigure'): _s.reconfigure(errors='replace')`. Linux output stays identical because UTF-8 encodes everything. Workaround without code changes: `$env:PYTHONUTF8='1'` in PowerShell before launching; the bake child and spawn workers inherit it.

findings.mechanism: CPython 3.11 Lib/concurrent/futures/process.py defines `_MAX_WINDOWS_WORKERS = 63 - 2` and, on win32, raises `ValueError("max_workers must be <= 61")` for an explicit larger value (lines 664-667 in the 3.11 source I checked).
